body.en:
Inflation has dropped to 3.8% in the year to June, from 4% in the previous month, with lower than anticipated underlying price pressures weighing against the chance of another Reserve Bank interest rate hike.

The unexpected drop in headline inflation by the monthly measure was married with a softer than expected 0.8% quarterly increase in the RBA’s preferred trimmed mean measure of price growth, the Australian Bureau of Statistics data showed.

Before the latest inflation report, the chance of an 11 August hike had dwindled to 16%, from 50% on Friday, according to financial markets.

The latest consumer price figures come as Iran launched a volley of missiles at US bases in the region, puncturing days of calm and partially reversing some of the steep oil price falls over recent days.
body.zh: 截至 6 月份的一年中，通货膨胀率已从上个月的 4% 降至 3.8%，低于预期的潜在价格压力阻碍了储备银行再次加息的可能性。 澳大利亚统计局的数据显示，月度总体通胀率意外下降，同时澳洲联储首选的物价增长调整均值指标季度增幅低于预期（0.8%）。 根据金融市场的数据，在最新的通胀报告发布之前，8 月 11 日加息的可能性已从周五的 50% 降至 16%。 最新的消费者价格数据公布之际，伊朗向美国在该地区的基地发射了一系列导弹，打破了数日的平静，并部分扭转了近几天油价大幅下跌的趋势。

reflection.en: The successful completion of a marathon test flight highlights the meticulous planning and dedicated effort behind such a complex engineering feat. It reminds us that when we commit our endeavors to Yahweh, our plans can be established and brought to fruition.
reflection.zh: 这次马拉松式试飞的成功完成，彰显了如此复杂工程壮举背后一丝不苟的规划和专注的努力。它提醒我们，当我们把自己的事业交托给雅伟时，我们的计划就能得以确立并实现。

verse.textEn: Commit to Yahweh whatever you do, and he will establish your plans.
verse.textZh: 你所做的，要交托雅伟，你所谋的，就必成立。

title.en: Trump administration bans new Chinese humanoid robots
title.zh: 特朗普政府禁止新的中国类人机器人

summary.en: The US and China are locked in a race to lead the world in robotics and artificial intelligence, with the Trump administration banning new Chinese humanoid robots.
summary.zh: 美国和中国在机器人和人工智能领域展开全球领先地位的竞争，特朗普政府已禁止新的中国类人机器人。

body.en:
The Trump administration on Tuesday announced a ban on new foreign-made humanoid robot imports to the US over "unacceptable risks" to the country's national security.

The move applies to advanced robots - including humanoid and four-legged machines. Many of them are made in China, which is locked in a race with the US to develop robotics and artificial intelligence (AI).

The Federal Communications Commission (FCC) also banned the import of power inverters - a device used in data centres and solar panels - which it said could also pose a risk to the US economy.

FCC chairman Brendan Carr said the agency was doing its part "to secure America's critical supply chains".

The BBC has contacted the Chinese embassy in Washington as well as major Chinese robot manufacturers Unitree, UBTech and AgiBot.

The FCC has added the items to its Covered List - a register of goods and services that are deemed a risk to US national security.

The ban applies to new foreign-produced advanced robotic devices and power inverters and does not prevent the sale or import of any existing models that had been previously authorised by the FCC.

The FCC cited concerns that the use of foreign-made inverters could allow overseas firms to turn them off, steal data, facilitate remote access and surveillance by "foreign government actors, or be otherwise exploited through a cyberattack."

It added that the use of robots made outside the US could allow "malign actors to surveil Americans, enhance the capabilities of foreign intelligence services, or to remotely commandeer the robots."

China's exports have come under intense scrutiny by the US as the Trump administration attempts to address trade imbalances with the world's second largest economy.

Despite being the world's biggest exporter of electric vehicles, China has been effectively shut out of the American market by a steep tariff.

Washington has also blocked the sale of cutting-edge US semiconductors to China in a bid to protect national security, slow Beijing's military modernisation and maintain America's lead in AI.

US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has also warned that Chinese AI firms could face sanctions over allegations that they have stolen American intellectual property .

In response the Chinese government has said its country's development of AI was "the result of its own dedication and effort as well as international cooperation".

Chinese technology firms have rapidly developed humanoid robots to be used in settings including factories and homes.

Companies have also been quick to market their machines to businesses and the public ahead of US humanoid robot rivals like Elon Musk's Tesla and Boston Dynamics.
body.zh: 特朗普政府周二宣布禁止向美国进口新的外国制造的人形机器人，理由是该机器人对美国国家安全构成“不可接受的风险”。 这一举措适用于先进的机器人——包括人形机器人和四足机器人。其中许多是中国制造的，中国正在与美国展开机器人和人工智能（AI）开发竞赛。 美国联邦通信委员会（FCC）还禁止进口逆变器（一种用于数据中心和太阳能电池板的设备），并表示这也可能对美国经济构成风险。 FCC 主席布伦丹·卡尔表示，该机构正在尽自己的一份力量“确保美国关键供应链的安全”。 BBC已联系中国驻华盛顿大使馆以及中国主要机器人制造商Unitree、UBTech和AgiBot。 美国联邦通信委员会已将这些物品添加到其涵盖清单中，即被视为对美国国家安全构成风险的商品和服务的登记册。 该禁令适用于新的外国生产的先进机器人设备和电源逆变器，并不阻止销售或进口此前已获得 FCC 授权的任何现有型号。 美国联邦通信委员会担心，使用外国制造的逆变器可能会导致海外公司关闭逆变器、窃取数据、促进“外国政府行为者”的远程访问和监视，或者通过网络攻击而被利用。 它补充说，使用美国境外制造的机器人可能会导致“恶意行为者监视美国人，增强外国情报部门的能力，或远程征用机器人。” 随着特朗普政府试图解决与世界第二大经济体的贸易不平衡问题，中国的出口受到美国的严格审查。 尽管中国是世界上最大的电动汽车出口国，但由于高额关税，中国实际上被排除在美国市场之外。 华盛顿还阻止向中国出售美国尖端半导体，以保护国家安全、减缓北京的军事现代化进程并保持美国在人工智能领域的领先地位。 美国财政部长斯科特·贝森特也警告说，中国人工智能公司可能因涉嫌窃取美国知识产权而面临制裁。 作为回应，中国政府表示，中国人工智能的发展是“自身奉献和努力以及国际合作的结果”。 中国科技公司迅速开发出用于工厂和家庭等环境的人形机器人。 公司也迅速向企业和公众推销他们的机器，领先于埃隆·马斯克(Elon Musk)的特斯拉和波士顿动力公司等美国人形机器人竞争对手。

reflection.en: This global race for technological supremacy echoes humanity's ancient drive to build and achieve great things, as seen in the ambition to build a tower to the heavens. While innovation can bring progress, the pursuit of ultimate leadership can sometimes reflect a desire for human glory rather than a humble stewardship of creation. Yahweh reminds us that...
reflection.zh: 这场全球科技霸权之争，与人类自古以来建造宏伟工程、追求卓越的冲动不谋而合，正如建造通天塔的雄心。虽然创新能带来进步，但对终极领导地位的追求有时可能反映出对人类荣耀的渴望，而非对受造物的谦卑管理。雅伟提醒我们，真正的智慧在于认识到我们的局限，并在我们所有的努力中寻求祂的指引。

verse.textEn: Yahweh said, 'If as one people speaking the same language they have begun to do this, then nothing they plan to do will be impossible for them.'
verse.textZh: 雅伟说：「看哪，他们成为一样的人民，都是一样的言语，如今既做起这事来，以后他们所要做的事就没有不成就的了。」

title.en: Iran and US trade strikes, shattering brief lull in fighting
title.zh: 伊朗和美国的贸易打击打破了短暂的战斗平静

summary.en: US Central Command says it intercepted "multiple" ballistic missiles fired by Iran.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及管家责任、供应与公共福祉。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Iran has launched "multiple" ballistic missiles in an "attempted surprise attack" on American forces in the Middle East, the US military said, shattering a lull in the fighting.

The attack occurred at 17:45 EDT (21:45 GMT) on Tuesday, with all missiles "successfully intercepted", said US Central Command (Centcom), which did not disclose any locations of targets.

The US military and Saudi Arabian forces meanwhile struck "Iran-aligned terrorists" in Iraq in retaliation for Iran-directed drone attacks, according to Centcom.

Tehran has not yet commented. The reported crossfire would end a brief break in hostilities between the US and Iran, which was designed to bring negotiators back to the table.

The US and Saudi Arabia struck "multiple terrorist logistics and weapons sites" in eastern Iraq, according to Centcom.

The US military said this was "a strong response to over 30 IRGC-directed aerial drone attacks in the last 72 hours", using an acronym for Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps.

Centcom said Iran's military "and its terrorist proxies must cease these attacks to avoid further US military response".

Earlier on Tuesday, Saudi Arabia said its military had intercepted and destroyed drones targeting petroleum facilities in the country's eastern region.

Defence ministry spokesman Major General Turki al-Maliki alleged the drones were launched by Iran-affiliated militia groups in Iraqi territory.

The reignited hostilities come a day after US President Donald Trump spoke of "very friendly negotiations" with Iran. At that point, the two sides had not exchanged strikes for a third consecutive day.

Access and control of the Strait of Hormuz remains a key sticking point in talks, which Tehran has denied are even happening.

The latest strikes coincided with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's visit to Washington, where he met Trump at the White House and attended the funeral of US Senator Lindsey Graham, a prominent Iran hawk.

At least 624 US military service members have been wounded since Trump ordered strikes against Iran in February, according to recent Pentagon data.

The Pentagon said 417 of those personnel were injured in relation to Operation Epic Fury, the joint US-Israeli military operation against Iran.
body.zh: 美国军方表示，伊朗发射了“多枚”弹道导弹，对驻中东的美军进行“企图突然袭击”，打破了战斗的平静。 美国中央司令部 (Centcom) 表示，此次袭击发生在周二美国东部时间 17:45（格林尼治标准时间 21:45），所有导弹均“被成功拦截”，但未透露任何目标位置。 据中央司令部称，美国军方和沙特阿拉伯军队同时在伊拉克打击了“与伊朗结盟的恐怖分子”，以报复伊朗指挥的无人机袭击。 德黑兰尚未发表评论。据报道，此次交火将结束美国和伊朗之间短暂的敌对行动，此举旨在让谈判代表重返谈判桌。 据中央司令部称，美国和沙特阿拉伯袭击了伊拉克东部的“多个恐怖分子后勤和武器基地”。 美国军方表示，这是“对过去 72 小时内 IRGC 指挥的 30 多次无人机袭击的强烈回应”，美国军方使用的是伊朗伊斯兰革命卫队的缩写。 中央司令部表示，伊朗军方“及其恐怖分子代理人必须停止这些袭击，以避免美国进一步采取军事反应”。 周二早些时候，沙特阿拉伯表示，其军方拦截并摧毁了针对该国东部地区石油设施的无人机。 国防部发言人图尔基·马利基少将声称，这些无人机是由伊朗附属民兵组织在伊拉克境内发射的。 就在美国总统唐纳德·特朗普表示与伊朗进行“非常友好的谈判”的第二天，敌对行动重新燃起。至此，双方已经连续第三天没有交锋。 霍尔木兹海峡的进入和控制仍然是谈判的一个关键症结所在，德黑兰否认这种情况正在发生。 最近的袭击恰逢以色列总理本杰明·内塔尼亚胡访问华盛顿，他在白宫会见了特朗普，并参加了著名的伊朗鹰派美国参议员林赛·格雷厄姆的葬礼。 五角大楼最近的数据显示，自特朗普 2 月份下令对伊朗发动袭击以来，至少有 624 名美国军人受伤。 五角大楼表示，其中 417 名人员在美以针对伊朗的联合军事行动“史诗愤怒行动”中受伤。

title.en: How Mexican drug cartels have outsourced meth labs to Nigeria
title.zh: 墨西哥贩毒集团如何将冰毒实验室外包给尼日利亚

summary.en: West Africa is becoming increasingly attractive to those who want to make and export illicit drugs.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及和平与克制。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
The Nigerian judge was formally dressed, the lawyers maintained legal decorum and protocol was followed – but this hearing was not in the comfortable confines of a Lagos courtroom, it was inside an alleged illicit drug laboratory in the thick of a dense forest.

Three Mexicans and seven Nigerians were paraded in handcuffs, as Justice Musa Kakaki inspected the chemicals and equipment they were accused of using to produce the harmful illegal synthetic drug, methamphetamine, commonly known as meth, crystal meth or, locally, ice.

A bitter, pungent smell filled the air of the makeshift laboratory, thanks to a large drum of the liquid form of the drug that was crystallising. Another potent odour came from open vats of a dark, viscous liquid, described as "crude", or unprocessed, methamphetamine.

Other products were scattered around, including propane gas cylinders and bags of caustic soda, in the unfinished building.

This temporary move of the federal high court to a location a two-hour drive from Lagos was an unusual step for Nigeria's judicial system, but the National Drug Law Enforcement Agency (NDLEA) said it was necessary to understand the scale of the operation.

When the suspects were arrested in May, the agency described it as the country's largest-ever meth bust. It said it discovered more than two tonnes of the drug worth some $360m (£270m).

The NDLEA at the time announced it had "dealt another crippling blow" and dismantled "a highly sophisticated, multi-million-dollar Nigerian-Mexican methamphetamine production syndicate".

The following month, agents found another meth laboratory hidden in a forest in neighbouring Oyo State.

That time they arrested five suspects, including one Mexican "methamphetamine expert".

The raids underline a broader trend of Africa's, and particularly West Africa's, growing role in the global synthetic drugs ⁠trade and the shift by criminal cartels to use the continent, not just as a trafficking hub, but also as a production base.

Mexican specialists in manufacturing methamphetamine, often described as "cooks", are increasingly being found working alongside locals in laboratories in Europe and Africa, according to law-enforcement agencies.

Meth production has become increasingly sophisticated over the last few decades.

"They perfected it, to the point now it is the highest purity, the highest potency version of meth," James Griego, who leads counter-narcotics operations for US-Africa Command (Africom), told the BBC.

Africom, which oversees US military operations on the continent, has provided several national anti-drug organisations with intelligence to assist with their raids.

"Anybody who is looking to consume methamphetamine, understands that the Mexican meth is the best in the world, for that purpose,"...

title.en: 'A lover of life' - Seattle pays tribute to food festival shooting victims
title.zh: “热爱生活”——西雅图向美食节枪击事件受害者致敬

summary.en: Families grieved on Monday as they remembered the three people killed in a shooting at a food festival.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及对脆弱群体的怜悯。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Much of the city of Seattle was in mourning on Monday as residents paid tribute to the three lives that were lost during a deadly street gunfight the day before.

The city's mayor was among dozens who gathered at a local fountain for a candlelight vigil, while online fundraisers for two of the victims received tens-of-thousands of dollars in donations.

Those who died on Sunday at the annual Bite of Seattle food festival were Junior Cee Niko Semo, 19, Carlos Israel Sanchez Villalba, 44, and Ashley Whitehead, 56. At least four others were injured.

A GoFundMe for Villalba described him as "a devoted husband, loving father of three, and a loyal friend who would do anything for anyone".

"His kindness and generosity touched countless lives, and everyone who knew him remembers his gentle spirit and willingness to help others," the write-up said.

"His sudden passing has left his family heartbroken and facing an uncertain future."

The family has said the funds will go towards funeral expenses and help fill the void in his absence. He leaves behind a wife and three children.

Sunday was the final day of the annual three-day free food festival, which draws some 350,000 people each year.

Family members of Ashley Whitehead said she was standing in line with her daughter, waiting for cotton candy, as gunshots rang out and ended her life.

She died in hospital during surgery, after exchanging "heartfelt 'I love you's with her eldest daughter", her family said in the GoFundMe page launched after her death.

"Family was everything to Ashley - she had recently moved to the west coast from Alabama to be closer to Zoie," the writeup said, referring to her eldest daughter.

At the vigil on Monday evening, people laid flowers and lit candles as they gathered in grief. There was a call for a moment of a silence.

"This is not acceptable," Seattle Mayor Katie Wilson said, condemning gun violence in the community. "No father, no parent should have to bury their child."

Washington state Governor Bob Ferguson said in a social media post that the community was shocked and "struggling to make sense of how an iconic community celebration could end in gunfire".

Police suspect the third deceased victim, Junior Cee Niko Semo, was involved in the gunfight. Neither of the other two victims are suspected of any crimes.

The authorities believe at least two other suspects were involved, including a 15-year-old, who is in custody, and a third unidentified person.

Police said at a news conference on Tuesday that the attack was a "targeted" act of gang violence. They are still investigating what groups may have been involved.

Three guns have been recovered from the scene of the shooting, including an unregistered "ghost gun" that has an extended 33-bullet magazine, and a pistol...

title.en: 'A narcissist' - victim's family blasts Kohberger for challenging Idaho murder conviction

summary.en: The man accused of killing four students in Idaho is taking back his plea, which was made to avoid the death penalty.

body.en:
The family of one of the victims of Bryan Kohberger has hit out after it emerged that he was challenging his conviction for four murders of students in the US state of Idaho.

Kohberger was sentenced last year to four consecutive terms of life in prison after pleading guilty to charges of murder in the November 2022 killings.

In recent days, Kohberger told the New York Times , external he was taking back his plea, which was made to avoid the death penalty. He said it had rested on "false promises and blatant disinformation".

The family of Kaylee Goncalves, one of the students who was killed, said that Kohberger was a "narcissist", who appeared to have changed his position.

"He chose not to leave his fate - or the facts of the case - to a jury," the statement from the Goncalves family said.

"He never cried foul, never claimed he was uninformed or pressured, and never suggested there were problems with the discovery materials he and his counsel had reviewed for two years that should have been challenged."

The Goncalves family went on to say "the real tragedy" was the amount of attention that Kohberger was now receiving at the expense of the victims.

Kohberger was convicted of stabbing to death housemates Kaylee Goncalves, Ethan Chapin, Xana Kernodle and Madison Mogen, who all attended the University of Idaho, in their off-campus home on 13 November 2022.

The case shocked the small student town of Moscow and made national headlines for almost two months before Kohberger was arrested.

Kohberger was a criminology doctorate student at a different institution, Washington State University.

He never shared a motive with the court and it is not clear why he drove to another campus to brutally stab four students.

Investigators were unable to link him to the victims, although they presented compelling evidence that put him at the scene of the crime.

In his statement to the New York Times, declaring his new intention to enter a not-guilty plea, Kohberger protested his innocence and said he was offering prosecutors another chance to file for the death penalty if they wanted to.

Idaho Attorney General Raúl Labrador paid tribute to the victims' families, saying they had "already endured unimaginable loss and now must face today's deeply painful news".

Labrador's statement added: "My office stands ready to do whatever is necessary to ensure justice is fully carried out."

"He told the judge under oath at the plea hearing that he understood the deal, was acting voluntarily, and was pleading guilty because he was guilty," Sam Newton, associate professor at University of Idaho College of Law, told the BBC.

body.en:
Spanish residents forced to flee some of the worst wildfires in living memory began returning to their homes on Wednesday, but thousands more were ordered to leave in France over fears that a looming heatwave would prevent containment of fires that have ripped through the country's southwest.

Swathes of tinder-dry forests, parched land and property have been destroyed west of the Spanish capital, Madrid, and in France's Gironde and Landes regions, forcing tens of thousands to head to safety.

Spain's interior ministry announced the end of evacuation orders for 13 municipalities on Tuesday afternoon local time, in rare good news for locals.

In the evacuated village of Navas del Rey, Reporters from the Agence France-Presse (AFP) news agency saw blackened debris, ash and burnt-out cars.

According to an initial estimate provided to AFP by municipal authorities, around 50 homes were destroyed by the flames and another 50 damaged.

Maria Paz Bolanos, 62, returned with her family to their home and garden in a housing development in the town — and found it only slightly scorched.

"We've been here 50 years," she said. "It must have been grandfather, my father in heaven. He somehow made it so the fire just came in through and stopped right there.

The mayor of nearby Pelayos de la Presa, Antonio Sin, described the scene as "a war zone".

"It has been a horrendous fire, a brutal one — it's a monster that has run over us," he told AFP.

In contrast, Marielle Mourgeon was among 4,000 people forced to cut short holidays in the French seaside village of Lacanau, in the Gironde area near Bordeaux, after camping sites were told to evacuate as a precaution.

"At first I thought my husband was joking, with the blue sky and the fires dying down," she said.

Over the past six days, the largest French wildfire since 1949 has raged west of Bordeaux , forcing more than 220,000 people to flee, destroying 240 houses and prompting questions about emergency preparedness.

Sophie Brocas, the government's top official in Gironde, told reporters the fire had "stabilised... meaning it is not advancing", and authorised nearly 60,000 people evacuated from three villages around the city to return.

South of Lege Cap Ferret on the Atlantic coast, volunteers have been working round the clock to help firefighters restock with water to tackle a wave of fires.

"We pour 8,000 litres on an area, and an hour later it starts up again," said one volunteer, Pierre Marie, after a 12-hour day.

title.en: Trump voices irritation with Netanyahu as relations with Zelenskyy warm
title.zh: 特朗普对内塔尼亚胡表示不满，与泽连斯基的关系升温

summary.en: Reports indicate a shift in former President Trump's international relationships, with his ties to Ukrainian President Zelenskyy improving while his relationship with Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu shows increasing signs of strain.
summary.zh: 有报道称，美国前总统特朗普的国际关系正在发生变化，他与乌克兰总统泽连斯基的关系有所改善，而与以色列总理内塔尼亚胡的关系则持续出现紧张迹象。

body.en:
US President Donald Trump voiced irritation with Benjamin Netanyahu ahead of their White House meeting on Wednesday, complaining that details of the Israeli prime minister's planned talking points on Iran had surfaced publicly, in a fresh sign of strain between the two leaders.

Asked about reports that Netanyahu wanted to talk to him about Pickaxe Mountain, a fortified facility buried deep underground near one of Iran's main nuclear sites, Trump said, using Netanyahu's nickname, "I don't need Bibi to tell me that. Bibi's telling me that because he wants me to stay involved."

"Why don't you just tell it to me? Why do you have to announce it to the world?" Trump said in an interview with the television program Fox & Friends.

The New York Post reported on Monday, citing a source in Jerusalem, that Netanyahu was expected to provide intelligence to Trump that Iran is building up its nuclear facilities at Pickaxe Mountain and is lying about wanting a peace deal.

In a video released on social media following the meeting, however, Netanyahu described the meeting as "excellent" and "one of the best conversations" he has had with Trump.

"It was a conversation marked by full partnership, mutual support and a shared understanding of our common objective: to ensure that Iran does not obtain nuclear weapons, as well as other goals," he said.

Photos posted by Netanyahu's office on X showed the two leaders sitting beside each other in the Oval Office with wide smiles. They were joined by vice president JD Vance, secretary of state Marco Rubio and defence secretary Pete Hegseth.

Trump met Netanyahu after first having brief closed-door talks with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy.

White House press secretary Karoline Leavitt described both meetings as "positive and productive."

Relations with Zelenskyy have warmed as Ukraine has blunted Russian advances in their more than four-year-old war, while Netanyahu faces growing White House frustration over the lack of progress toward a broader settlement in the Iran conflict and criticism from some of Trump's supporters who oppose deeper US involvement in the Middle East.

The Israeli and Ukrainian leaders were in Washington to attend a memorial service for US Senator Lindsey Graham, a hawkish Republican who was an influential advocate for both Israel and Ukraine in the US capital.

Both the Ukraine war and the widening Middle East conflict are at critical junctures. After the collapse of a ceasefire in the Iran war, Trump says he has paused US airstrikes to give diplomacy another chance. Zelenskyy, meanwhile, has been buoyed by Ukraine's recent successes.

title.en: Where Australia sits in this $6 billion race for influence as China's strategy shifts

summary.en: What was a "real foothold" for China in the Pacific has been narrowed, according to a new report.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及真理、分辨与诚实。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Australia has continued to outrank China as the Pacific's biggest source of development aid, contributing a third of loans and infrastructure investment to the region, according to a new report.

Looking at development projects across the Pacific between 2008 and 2024, the Lowy Institute report found that, after years of decline, aid to the region increased by 10 per cent in 2024.

Total development aid stood at US$4.1 billion ($5.85 billion) in that year, but the report's authors estimate that would drop to US$3.8 billion ($5.42 billion) in yet-to-be-released 2025 figures.

With China now shifting strategy from big debt-fuelled loans to smaller strategic aid, and amid major economic shocks in the Pacific, the contest for regional influence is coming under greater strain.

Australia was the Pacific's biggest donor in 2024, giving $2.14 billion in aid, which made up 37 per cent of all finance to the region in that year.

A total of $6 billion in financing was dispensed from New Zealand, China, and regional development banks.

Australia has also inked $3.4 billion in loan deals, ending China's reign as the region's leading lender.

"That's a product of many years of Australia pushing into these spaces, but it's meant that what was once a real foothold for China in the region has been narrowed," the report's lead author Riley Duke told SBS News.

"Australia is consistently providing the most grant financing to the region, and that picture hasn't really changed."

The report, released on Tuesday, says demand for Chinese loans has dropped since 2019 due to concerns about servicing the debt, more competition between lenders and Chinese banks' capital availability.

Australia is also a major financier of climate change mitigation projects in the Pacific, including a solar and battery storage facility for Palau to help generate 20 per cent of its electricity, and Tonga's Renewable Energy Stabilisation Package.

The fruits of those efforts have paid off for Australia, with a flurry of regional security deals announced in recent months, including with Fiji, Vanuatu , Papua New Guinea and Tuvalu.

"They are a clear marker of Australia establishing itself as the lead partner to the region," Duke said.

"Those deals ... take a long time to progress. They're complicated, but they reflect Australia establishing itself as an inalienably important partner to Pacific countries."

Developing Pacific Island nations have been hit hard by multiple shocks, including the COVID-19 pandemic and more recently, fuel supply shortages caused by the United States-Israeli war on Iran.

title.en: Fujimori takes charge in Peru amid China, US balancing act
title.zh: 藤森在中美平衡之际掌管秘鲁

summary.en: Peru's new president, Keiko Fujimori, has promised more security and investment. Now in office, she'll have to find space for the South American nation amid Washington and Beijing's geopolitical rivalry.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及领导、智慧与公共责任。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Peru's new president, Keiko Fujimori, has promised more security and investment. Now in office, she'll have to find space for the South American nation amid Washington and Beijing's geopolitical rivalry.

Keiko Fujimori's swearing in on Tuesday marked the return of a political movement that had been out of power for more than a quarter century.

Fujimorism, a mix of neoliberalism, populism and strict government policies, characterized the 1990-2000 presidency of her father, the late Alberto Fujimori. Keiko Fujimori is stepping in amid a climate of social polarization, with promises to deliver more security, economic recovery and improvements in the health and education sectors.

But beyond those domestic projects, Fujimori is taking charge at a time of increased strategic importance for Peru . The country has become one of the key battlegrounds in the growing competition between the United States and China for political influence in South America.

Fujimori has already signaled that security will be the top priority for her government.

On the agenda: more video surveillance, a stronger police presence, tougher punishment for crimes and organized gangs, and command and control centers across the country. Part of the crackdown includes the construction of four mega-prisons, like those in El Salvador .

Eliana Carlin, a political science expert at the Pontifical Catholic University of Peru in Lima, is concerned by how Fujimori's plans will affect human rights .

"Behind [these measures] lie strong ideological positions intended to justify making the police and the armed forces solely subject to military jurisdiction," she said.

In addition to a stronger focus on security, Fujimori has said she intends to advance infrastructure projects, attract private investment, build new schools and hospitals and modernize the country with the help of technology and artificial intelligence .

But delivering on these pledges depends largely on whether the government can find the necessary funds. Infrastructure and essential services continue to face significant deficits. Added to that is the surging crime rate and the threat of the strengthening El Nino weather pattern , which could hit Peru with increased drought, extreme heat , flooding and other climate-related disruptions.

Foreign policy is also a major challenge for Fujimori's administration. The opening of the Chancay port and logistics hub has turned Peru into a strategic player in regional trade — and made it a central focus in the geopolitical rivalry between Washington and Beijing.

title.en: EU civil protection mechanism: Coordinating Europe's firefighters
title.zh: 欧盟民事保护机制：协调欧洲消防员

summary.en: French President Emmanuel Macron has activated the EU civil protection mechanism to help combat devastating wildfires. The system has become increasingly effective, yet it will reach its limits in the summer of 2026.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及领导、智慧与公共责任。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
French President Emmanuel Macron has activated the EU civil protection mechanism to help combat devastating wildfires. The system has become increasingly effective, yet it will reach its limits in the summer of 2026.

France is quite well-prepared for wildfires. The government operates 12 Canadair water bombers and eight Dash firefighting aircraft. In addition, leased aircraft and helicopters are being used.

However, the fleet is currently needed simultaneously across many parts of the country. A drought has been intensifying for weeks, and several heat waves with temperatures sometimes exceeding 40 degrees Celsius (104 Fahrenheit) have left the vegetation extremely parched. The devastating wildfire near Bordeaux on the Atlantic coast has already engulfed more than 42,000 hectares of forest and vegetation.

At the same time, fires and follow-up extinguishing efforts in southern and southeastern France  are tying up additional emergency personnel. In many places, firefighters are battling the flames in an exhausting, round-the-clock effort. However, strong winds are fanning the fire fronts, making them almost unstoppable, and more than 220,000 people have had to leave their homes and vacation homes so far.

The gravity of the situation is also underscored by the fact that the French government has deployed an A400M military transport aircraft equipped for aerial firefighting for the first time. The A400M can drop around 20 metric tons of fire retardant, more than three times as much as a Canadair.

Nevertheless, the situation is currently so dire that President Emmanuel Macron also activated the EU civil protection mechanism (CPM) and requested assistance from other European countries.

To activate the CPM, a country reports its needs to the European Union's emergency response coordination centre, ERCC, in Brussels . ERCC experts assess which of the 37 participating countries can provide assistance.

Initial assistance for France was mobilized within a few hours and has since been significantly expanded. Firefighting aircraft and helicopters from Portugal , Croatia , the Czech Republic , Germany , Turkey , Sweden  and Slovakia  are supporting France, primarily in the greater Bordeaux area.

At the same time, however, the EU also dispatched six additional firefighting aircraft from Greece , Turkey and Italy to Spain . This means that 13 of the 22 firefighting aircraft available for this summer have already been mobilized for these two countries. The figures also demonstrate how quickly the European reserve can be drawn upon when multiple large-scale wildfires occur simultaneously. title.en: Could US airstrikes stop insurgency in Mali?
title.zh: 美国空袭能否阻止马里叛乱？

summary.en: US President Donald Trump is reportedly considering airstrikes against the Al-Qaeda-linked JNIM in Mali. Analysts suggest that while such attacks might weaken the jihadist group, they would not resolve the underlying core issues of the conflict.
summary.zh: 据多方报道，美国总统唐纳德·特朗普正在考虑对马里与基地组织有关联的JNIM发动空袭。分析人士指出，此类袭击或许能削弱圣战分子，但无法解决核心问题。

body.en:
US President Donald Trump is considering airstrikes against the Al-Qaeda-linked JNIM in Mali, according to multiple reports. Analysts say such attacks might weaken the jihadists but would not address the core issues.

For years, Mali has struggled to contain a growing jihadist insurgency , particularly in the country's northern region. Following the withdrawal of French troops and despite the authorities' close cooperation with Russia , the al-Qaeda-linked Jama'at Nusrat al-Islam wal-Muslimin (JNIM) continues to expand its influence. Now, a new actor could enter the conflict: the United States (US) .

Founded in 2017, JNIM unites several Islamist groups under the banner of al-Qaeda . Over the past years, the organization has developed into the most powerful jihadist force in the Sahel . Its objective is the establishment of an Islamist order and the displacement of state structures as well as Western influence.

"We are no longer talking about a group that only carries out isolated attacks," explains Tobias Rüttershof, head of the Sahel Program of the Konrad Adenauer Foundation (KAS), which is affiliated with Germany's CDU party and has an office in Mali, in an interview with DW. "In many regions, JNIM effectively controls the security situation, collects taxes, mediates local conflicts and in some areas is more present than the Malian state." 

According to the US National Counterterrorism Center, JNIM was responsible for more than 1,200 deaths in 2025, making it the second-deadliest terrorist organization in the world. Particularly concerning is the group's geographic expansion: JNIM is now active not only in Burkina Faso and Niger , but increasingly in the coastal states of West Africa. 

The US government is divided over the question of direct military strikes. Supporters such as Sebastian Gorka, senior director for counterterrorism at the National Security Council, argue that JNIM is one of the world's most dangerous jihadist organizations and that its advance must be halted.

Russia's security strategy in Mali has so far failed to deliver results, according to Rüttershof. 

"After the withdrawal of French forces, the UN mission MINUSMA , and European training missions, Mali's military government argued that  Russia could stabilize the security situation more effectively," Gorka told DW. "That expectation has not been fulfilled so far. On the contrary, JNIM appears stronger today than it was several years ago."

Following military coups in 2020 and 2021, Bamako increasingly distanced itself from Western partners and expanded cooperation with Russia.

The Malian government has responded cautiously to reports of possible US airstrikes.

title.en: Tsunami warnings issued for southern Japan after major earthquake

summary.en: An earthquake struck Japan's southern Kyushu island, leading to thousands of homes losing power and the issuance of a tsunami warning.
summary.zh: 日本南部九州岛发生地震，导致数千户家庭停电，并发布了海啸警报。

body.en:
An earthquake with a preliminary magnitude of ‌7.1 has struck Japan's southern Kumamoto prefecture, knocking out power to ‌thousands of homes, stopping rail services and triggering warnings for tsunamis and ‌aftershocks.

Companies including Sony and TSMC, the world's largest contract chipmaker, have plants in the area of the quake.

The ‌Japanese government ‌issued emergency ⁠earthquake warnings on Tuesday for Kumamoto, Nagasaki, Kagoshima, Fukuoka, Saga, Oita, and Miyazaki prefectures, all on Japan's southern Kyushu island.

A tsunami warning for a wave measuring one metre was briefly issued after the earthquake, the Japan Meteorological Agency said.

Japan is one of the world's most earthquake-prone ⁠countries, with a tremor occurring at ‌least every five minutes.

Located along the "Ring of Fire" of volcanoes and oceanic trenches partly encircling ‌th Pacific Basin, Japan accounts for about 20 per cent of the world's earthquakes of magnitude 6.0 or more.

A massive earthquake in Kumamoto 10 years ago killed 275 people and injured a further 2739, according to an official count.

Kyushu Electric Power said about 40,000 homes ‌had lost power as a result of the quake, while railway company JR Kyushu said it had suspended services, including its high-speed bullet trains.

title.en: Trump administration bans new Chinese humanoid robots
title.zh: 特朗普政府禁止新型中国人形机器人

summary.en: The US and China are locked in a race to the lead the world in robotics and artificial intelligence.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自中国栏目的新闻，重点涉及和平与克制。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
The Trump administration on Tuesday announced a ban on new foreign-made humanoid robot imports to the US over "unacceptable risks" to the country's national security.

The move applies to advanced robots - including humanoid and four-legged machines. Many of them are made in China, which is locked in a race with the US to develop robotics and artificial intelligence (AI).

The Federal Communications Commission (FCC) also banned the import of power inverters - a device used in data centres and solar panels - which it said could also pose a risk to the US economy.

FCC chairman Brendan Carr said the agency was doing its part "to secure America's critical supply chains".

The BBC has contacted the Chinese embassy in Washington as well as major Chinese robot manufacturers Unitree, UBTech and AgiBot.

The FCC has added the items to its Covered List - a register of goods and services that are deemed a risk to US national security.

The ban applies to new foreign-produced advanced robotic devices and power inverters and does not prevent the sale or import of any existing models that had been previously authorised by the FCC.

The FCC cited concerns that the use of foreign-made inverters could allow overseas firms to turn them off, steal data, facilitate remote access and surveillance by "foreign government actors, or be otherwise exploited through a cyberattack."

It added that the use of robots made outside the US could allow "malign actors to surveil Americans, enhance the capabilities of foreign intelligence services, or to remotely commandeer the robots."

China's exports have come under intense scrutiny by the US as the Trump administration attempts to address trade imbalances with the world's second largest economy.

Despite being the world's biggest exporter of electric vehicles, China has been effectively shut out of the American market by a steep tariff.

Washington has also blocked the sale of cutting-edge US semiconductors to China in a bid to protect national security, slow Beijing's military modernisation and maintain America's lead in AI.

US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has also warned that Chinese AI firms could face sanctions over allegations that they have stolen American intellectual property .

In response the Chinese government has said its country's development of AI was "the result of its own dedication and effort as well as international cooperation".

Chinese technology firms have rapidly developed humanoid robots to be used in settings including factories and homes.

Companies have also been quick to market their machines to businesses and the public ahead of US humanoid robot rivals like Elon Musk's Tesla and Boston Dynamics.
body.zh: 特朗普政府周二宣布禁止向美国进口新的外国制造的人形机器人，理由是该机器人对美国国家安全构成“不可接受的风险”。 这一举措适用于先进的机器人——包括人形机器人和四足机器人。其中许多是中国制造的，中国正在与美国展开机器人和人工智能（AI）开发竞赛。 美国联邦通信委员会（FCC）还禁止进口逆变器（一种用于数据中心和太阳能电池板的设备），并表示这也可能对美国经济构成风险。 FCC 主席布伦丹·卡尔表示，该机构正在尽自己的一份力量“确保美国关键供应链的安全”。 BBC已联系中国驻华盛顿大使馆以及中国主要机器人制造商Unitree、UBTech和AgiBot。 美国联邦通信委员会已将这些物品添加到其涵盖清单中，即被视为对美国国家安全构成风险的商品和服务的登记册。 该禁令适用于新的外国生产的先进机器人设备和电源逆变器，并不阻止销售或进口此前已获得 FCC 授权的任何现有型号。 美国联邦通信委员会担心，使用外国制造的逆变器可能会导致海外公司关闭逆变器、窃取数据、促进“外国政府行为者”的远程访问和监视，或者通过网络攻击而被利用。 它补充说，使用美国境外制造的机器人可能会导致“恶意行为者监视美国人，增强外国情报部门的能力，或远程征用机器人。” 随着特朗普政府试图解决与世界第二大经济体的贸易不平衡问题，中国的出口受到美国的严格审查。 尽管中国是世界上最大的电动汽车出口国，但由于高额关税，中国实际上被排除在美国市场之外。 华盛顿还阻止向中国出售美国尖端半导体，以保护国家安全、减缓北京的军事现代化进程并保持美国在人工智能领域的领先地位。 美国财政部长斯科特·贝森特也警告说，中国人工智能公司可能因涉嫌窃取美国知识产权而面临制裁。 作为回应，中国政府表示，中国人工智能的发展是“自身奉献和努力以及国际合作的结果”。 中国科技公司迅速开发出用于工厂和家庭等环境的人形机器人。 公司也迅速向企业和公众推销他们的机器，领先于埃隆·马斯克(Elon Musk)的特斯拉和波士顿动力公司等美国人形机器人竞争对手。

body.en:
Australia has continued to outrank China as the Pacific's biggest source of development aid, contributing a third of loans and infrastructure investment to the region, according to a new report.

Looking at development projects across the Pacific between 2008 and 2024, the Lowy Institute report found that, after years of decline, aid to the region increased by 10 per cent in 2024.

Total development aid stood at US$4.1 billion ($5.85 billion) in that year, but the report's authors estimate that would drop to US$3.8 billion ($5.42 billion) in yet-to-be-released 2025 figures.

With China now shifting strategy from big debt-fuelled loans to smaller strategic aid, and amid major economic shocks in the Pacific, the contest for regional influence is coming under greater strain.

Australia was the Pacific's biggest donor in 2024, giving $2.14 billion in aid, which made up 37 per cent of all finance to the region in that year.

A total of $6 billion in financing was dispensed from New Zealand, China, and regional development banks.

Australia has also inked $3.4 billion in loan deals, ending China's reign as the region's leading lender.

"That's a product of many years of Australia pushing into these spaces, but it's meant that what was once a real foothold for China in the region has been narrowed," the report's lead author Riley Duke told SBS News.

"Australia is consistently providing the most grant financing to the region, and that picture hasn't really changed."

The report, released on Tuesday, says demand for Chinese loans has dropped since 2019 due to concerns about servicing the debt, more competition between lenders and Chinese banks' capital availability.

Australia is also a major financier of climate change mitigation projects in the Pacific, including a solar and battery storage facility for Palau to help generate 20 per cent of its electricity, and Tonga's Renewable Energy Stabilisation Package.

The fruits of those efforts have paid off for Australia, with a flurry of regional security deals announced in recent months, including with Fiji, Vanuatu , Papua New Guinea and Tuvalu.

"They are a clear marker of Australia establishing itself as the lead partner to the region," Duke said.

"Those deals ... take a long time to progress. They're complicated, but they reflect Australia establishing itself as an inalienably important partner to Pacific countries."

summary.en: Activists under threat from Beijing are facing strange difficulties with UK immigration. Their safety must not be traded for warmer relations with China Nathan Law is a pro-democracy activist and former legislator from Hong Kong. He is currently a political refugee in the UK As...
summary.zh: 这是一则来自中国栏目的新闻，重点涉及公义、尊严与问责。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en: Activists under threat from Beijing are facing strange difficulties with UK immigration. Their safety must not be traded for warmer relations with China Nathan Law is a pro-democracy activist and former legislator from Hong Kong. He is currently a political refugee in the UK As authoritarian countries such as Russia, China and Iran are more active in engaging in long-arm strategies to silence their critics in the UK, transnational repression is garnering more attention. It is right that the Metropolitan police and other British law enforcement agencies have specific units and mechanisms to counter it. But it takes more than just confronting this long-distance repression to make political dissidents of these authoritarian countries feel safe in the UK, and the UK government is not living up to expectations. The threat is real. Members of the Hongkonger community have received threats from the Chinese regime – some have had threatening letters, some people were deepfaked into sexual content, some even had families questioned and arrested back home. With the level of this targeting linked to the deterioration of Hong Kong politics, many have utilised the humanitarian pathway enabled by the previous government to relocate. Continue reading...
body.zh: 受到北京威胁的活动人士在英国移民问题上面临着奇怪的困难。不能用他们的安全来换取与中国关系的缓和。罗冠聪是一位民主活动人士，也是香港前立法会议员。他目前是英国的政治难民。随着俄罗斯、中国和伊朗等独裁国家更加积极地采取长臂战略来压制英国的批评者，跨国镇压正在引起更多关注。伦敦警察厅和其他英国执法机构确实有专门的单位和机制来应对。但要让这些独裁国家的政治异见人士在英国感到安全，仅仅面对这种远程镇压是不够的，而英国政府并没有达到人们的期望。威胁是真实的。香港人社区的成员受到了来自中国政权的威胁——有些人收到了恐吓信，有些人被深度伪造色情内容，有些人甚至在国内遭到盘问和逮捕。由于这种目标的程度与香港政治的恶化有关，许多人利用前任政府允许的人道主义途径搬迁。继续阅读...

reflection.en: This story draws attention to justice, dignity, and accountability. Micah 6:8 reminds us to meet sharp headlines with justice tempered by mercy, asking how faithful people can respond with wisdom instead of noise.
reflection.zh: 这则新闻让人想到公义、尊严与问责。Micah 6:8提醒我们，在快速变化的新闻里，仍要以带着怜悯的公义来回应，并学习用祷告与分辨代替情绪化判断。

title.en: Hong Kong activist allowed to stay in UK after deportation threat
title.zh: 香港活动人士在被驱逐出境威胁后获准留在英国

summary.en: Wu was detained for hours at London's Heathrow Airport last week and refused entry, he told the BBC.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自中国栏目的新闻，重点涉及和平与克制。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Former Hong Kong opposition leader Wu Chi-wai has been allowed to stay in the UK with his family for six months, after initially being detained at the border.

Wu had arrived at London's Heathrow Airport last Wednesday, where he was detained for nearly 10 hours and initially refused entry, he told BBC Chinese. He said he was later told he could stay for only one week, after which he would have to report to the airport to be deported.

But on Monday, the UK Border Force approved his entry and granted him a standard stay of six months, he said.

The 63-year-old was the leader of the now-defunct Democratic Party and one of the most recognisable faces of the city's quashed pro-democracy movement.

Wu is one of the so-called Hong Kong 47, a group of high-profile pro-democracy leaders who were sentenced to jail after a controversial national security trial.

He was released in June after spending more than five years in prison for subversion and other convictions.

Wu told BBC Chinese that his son and wife moved to the UK in 2022 and 2023, and the only communication he had with them since then was through monthly phone calls and letters. He had hoped to reunite with his family in the UK during his recent visit, he added.

Ahead of his departure, Wu said he had consulted staff at the British Consulate General in Hong Kong, asking if there would be any problems with his entry.

"The information I received was that there would be none," he said, adding that consular staff said they would explain his criminal record and itinerary to the UK Border Force.

The Border Force said he was not considered a "genuine visitor" who was solely visiting family, he said.

Wu denies that he had intended to apply for political asylum in the UK - a claim that was previously reported in the media.

Rights group Hong Kong Watch, which had called on UK authorities to allow Wu to stay in the country, said in a statement that it welcomed the recent news.

"This is the right outcome, and it should never have taken this long," Megan Khoo, Hong Kong Watch's policy director, said in a statement on Monday.

"He should never have faced the prospect of removal back to the city that jailed him."

Wu was using his British National (Overseas) (BNO) passport - a special travel document issued to Hong Kong permanent residents before 1 July 1997, when Hong Kong returned to Chinese rule - to enter the UK.

BNO passport holders are typically allowed to stay in the UK visa-free for six months.

Since 2021, the UK government launched a visa programme for BNO passport holders. Those granted the visa are eligible to work, study and live in the UK, putting them on a pathway to citizenship after they settle in the UK.

The new policy came after Hong Kong was rocked by massive pro-democracy protests,...
body.zh: 香港前反对党领袖胡志伟最初在边境被拘留后，现已获准与家人在英国居留六个月。 吴告诉BBC中文网，他于上周三抵达伦敦希思罗机场，在那里被拘留了近10个小时，并最初被拒绝入境。他说，后来他被告知他只能停留一周，之后他必须到机场报到才能被驱逐出境。 但他说，周一，英国边境部队批准了他的入境，并给予他六个月的标准居留期限。 这位 63 岁的老人是现已解散的民主党领导人，也是该市被镇压的民主运动中最知名的面孔之一。 吴是所谓的“香港47人”之一，这是一群备受瞩目的亲民主领导人，他们在一次有争议的国家安全审判后被判入狱。 他因颠覆罪和其他罪名入狱五年多，并于六月获释。 吴告诉BBC中文，他的儿子和妻子于2022年和2023年移居英国，此后他与他们唯一的交流就是通过每月的电话和信件。他补充说，他希望在最近的访问期间与英国的家人团聚。 吴说，出发前曾咨询英国驻香港总领事馆工作人员，询问他入境是否会遇到任何问题。 他说：“我收到的信息是不会有任何人。”他补充说，领事馆工作人员表示，他们将向英国边境部队解释他的犯罪记录和行程。 他说，边防部队表示，他不被视为只是探望家人的“真正访客”。 吴否认他曾打算在英国申请政治庇护——此前媒体曾报道过这一说法。 人权组织“香港观察”曾呼吁英国当局允许吴留在该国，该组织在一份声明中表示，对最近的消息表示欢迎。 “这是正确的结果，不应该花这么长时间，”香港观察政策总监邱梅根 (Megan Khoo) 周一在一份声明中表示。 “他不应该面临被遣送回监禁他的城市的前景。” 吴当时使用他的英国国民（海外）（BNO）护照 - 1997年7月1日香港回归中国统治之前向香港永久居民签发的特殊旅行证件 - 进入英国。 BNO 护照持有者通常可以免签证在英国停留六个月。 自2021年起，英国政府针对BNO护照持有人推出了签证计划。获得签证的人有资格在英国工作、学习和生活，这使他们在英国定居后踏上了获得公民身份的途径。 这项新政策是在香港受到大规模民主抗议活动震动之后出台的……

reflection.en: This story draws attention to peace-making and restraint. Matthew 5:9 reminds us to meet sharp headlines with mercy, truth, and restraint, asking how faithful people can respond with wisdom instead of noise.
reflection.zh: 这则新闻让人想到和平与克制。Matthew 5:9提醒我们，在快速变化的新闻里，仍要以怜悯、真实与节制来回应，并学习用祷告与分辨代替情绪化判断。

verse.textEn: Blessed are the peacemakers, for they will be called children of God.
verse.textZh: 使人和睦的人有福了，因为他们必称为神的儿子。

title.en: ‘We have lost everything’: extreme rainfall across Asia brings flash floods and typhoons
title.zh: “我们失去了一切”：亚洲极端降雨引发山洪和台风

summary.en: Extreme rainfall across Asia has led to widespread flash floods and typhoons, causing immense devastation from Afghanistan to Taiwan. The unprecedented deluge highlights the severe impact of climate breakdown, with one construction worker describing 10 days and nights of non-stop rain and the loss of everything.
summary.zh: 亚洲各地遭遇极端降雨，引发大范围山洪和台风，从阿富汗到台湾都遭受了巨大破坏。这场前所未有的洪灾凸显了气候崩溃的毁灭性影响，一名建筑工人描述了连续十天十夜的降雨，以及他们失去了一切的困境。

body.en: From Afghanistan to Taiwan, unprecedented deluge highlights devastating impact of climate breakdown “It rained for 10 days and 10 nights, non-stop – I’d never seen anything like it,” says Anar Gul, a construction worker who lives in the remote district of Dur Baba in eastern Afghanistan. The houses in his village are built from stone and mud, which makes them extremely vulnerable to heavy rains. After days of rain, Gul’s kitchen collapsed and his neighbour, Sayed Afsar Sadat, saw a large part of his house completely destroyed. “Rains like this are coming heavier and earlier each year,” says Sadat. “They are destroying the roads and washing away our crops. It’s impacting us directly.” Continue reading...
body.zh: 从阿富汗到台湾，史无前例的洪水突显了气候崩溃的破坏性影响。居住在阿富汗东部杜巴巴偏远地区的建筑工人阿纳尔·古尔 (Anar Gul) 说：“这场雨持续了 10 天 10 夜，不间断，我从来没有见过这样的情况。”他村里的房子都是用石头和泥土建造的，这使得它们极易受到大雨的影响。经过几天的降雨，古尔的厨房倒塌了，他的邻居赛义德·阿夫萨·萨达特 (Sayed Afsar Sadat) 看到他的房子的很大一部分完全被毁。 “像这样的降雨每年都来得更大、更早，”萨达特说。 “他们毁坏了道路，冲走了我们的庄稼。这直接影响着我们。”继续阅读...

reflection.en: The widespread devastation from extreme rainfall across Asia reminds us of creation's deep distress. As the earth groans under the weight of unprecedented deluges, we are called to acknowledge the suffering of both the land and its inhabitants. In these moments of profound loss, we hold onto the hope that Yahweh hears the cries of creation and those who...
reflection.zh: 亚洲各地极端降雨造成的广泛破坏，提醒我们受造界正经历着深切的痛苦。当地球在史无前例的洪灾重压下呻吟时，我们被呼召去承认土地及其居民所承受的苦难。在这些深重损失的时刻，我们紧紧抓住雅伟垂听受造界和那些失去一切之人的呼求的盼望。

verse.textEn: We know that the whole creation has been groaning as in the pains of childbirth right up to the present time.
verse.textZh: 我们知道，一切受造之物一同叹息、劳苦，直到如今。

title.en: China's new challenge as natural disasters strike - fake AI videos
title.zh: 自然灾害来袭，虚假AI视频成中国新挑战

summary.en: Storms and flooding incidents over the last few months have seen fake AI-generated videos inundating social media in China.
summary.zh: 近几个月来，中国遭受了风暴和洪灾，导致社交媒体上充斥着大量人工智能生成的虚假视频。

body.en:
As China deals with the fallout of Typhoon Noul that made landfall over the weekend, officials will be painfully aware that they will likely have an additional challenge to deal with: dangerously misleading videos created with Artificial Intelligence (AI).

Powerful storms and flooding incidents over the last few months have seen fake videos inundating social media platforms – these include images of dead bodies floating in floodwaters, the false depiction of severe flooding in areas actually not affected and others with blatantly fake details of emergency response efforts.

In some areas, videos containing false information about power outages prompted residents to panic buy emergency supplies.

Flooding in Hengzhou city, Guangxi in early July caused hundreds of snakes to escape from a breeding farm. Then fake images were also published showing crocodiles being released into a river.

In an already tense and dangerous situation involving mass evacuations and complex rescue operations, authorities want to avoid panic. Now they fear that AI technology - which China is pouring billions of dollars into - is providing simple, accessible tools that can be used to trick the public.

"Many of these content creators use disaster news to try to gain followers, knowing that more sensational or exaggerated content will garner more likes and more views. They are deliberately fabricating information to grab people's attention," Huang Zhihua, Deputy Chief in charge of online public security for Zhejiang Police Department told Chinese state media.

In recent weeks, there have been arrests and punishment – ranging from detention awaiting criminal prosecution to fines – for the creation of bogus reports and video content.

But experts are warning that an unprecedented crisis of misinformation could be looming.

In an article published by the newspaper of the Communist Party's Central Party School, Professor Chen Bin said, "AI dramatically lowers the technical barriers to producing false information. Individuals no longer require sophisticated technical skills. By simply prompting AI tools, they can rapidly generate convincing text, images, audio and video… which is highly realistic but entirely fabricated content, manufactured on a large scale."

Professor Gao Fuping, from the East China University of Political Science and Law, told the BBC that motivation for the publishing of such false content ranges from those who do it "to create something amusing without thinking about the consequences", to those who want to "generate traffic for personal gain" or those who wish to deliberately "cause panic or social unrest".

"Some users think the online world is anonymous and unregulated or that they cannot be traced," he said.

body.zh: 当中国应对周末登陆的台风诺尔的影响时，官员们将痛苦地意识到他们可能还要应对额外的挑战：用人工智能（AI）制作的危险的误导性视频。 过去几个月发生的强烈风暴和洪水事件导致社交媒体平台上充斥着虚假视频——其中包括漂浮在洪水中的尸体的图像、对实际未受影响地区严重洪水的虚假描述，以及其他公然虚假的应急响应工作细节。 在一些地区，包含有关停电的虚假信息的视频促使居民恐慌购买应急物资。 7月初，广西衡州市发生洪水，导致数百条蛇从养殖场逃出。随后还发布了一些假图片，显示鳄鱼被释放到河里。 在涉及大规模疏散和复杂救援行动的紧张和危险局势中，当局希望避免恐慌。现在，他们担心中国正在投入数十亿美元的人工智能技术正在提供简单、易于使用的工具，可用于欺骗公众。 浙江省公安厅网络公安分管副局长黄志华对中国官方媒体表示，“许多内容创作者利用灾难新闻来吸引关注者，因为他们知道更耸人听闻或夸张的内容会获得更多点赞和浏览量。他们故意捏造信息来吸引人们的注意力。” 最近几周，有人因制作虚假报告和视频内容而遭到逮捕和处罚，从等待刑事起诉的拘留到罚款。 但专家警告说，一场前所未有的错误信息危机可能即将来临。 陈斌教授在中共中央党校报刊发表的文章中表示，“人工智能极大地降低了制造虚假信息的技术门槛，个人不再需要高深的技术技能，只需人工智能工具的提示，就可以快速生成令人信服的文字、图像、音频和视频……这些内容高度真实，但完全是捏造的、大规模制造的内容。” 华东政法大学教授高福平告诉BBC，发布此类虚假内容的动机包括“为了制造一些有趣的事情而不考虑后果”，到“为个人利益产生流量”或故意“引起恐慌或社会动荡”。 “一些用户认为网络世界是匿名的、不受监管的，或者他们无法被追踪，”他说。 有人呼吁所有人工智能生成的......

reflection.en: In times of crisis, when natural disasters strike, the rapid spread of misinformation, especially through fake AI videos, can add to public distress. Proverbs 14:15 reminds us to be discerning, not simply believing everything we encounter, but thoughtfully considering the information before us. Cultivating prudence helps us navigate a complex digital...
reflection.zh: 在危机时期，当自然灾害发生时，虚假信息，特别是人工智能生成的虚假视频的迅速传播，会增加公众的痛苦。箴言14:15提醒我们要有辨别力，不要轻易相信我们所遇到的一切，而是要审慎思考摆在我们面前的信息。培养审慎的态度有助于我们驾驭复杂的数字环境，并明智地应对挑战。

verse.textEn: The simple believe anything, but the prudent give thought to their steps.
verse.textZh: 愚蒙人是话都信；通达人步步谨慎。

title.en: US-China AI rivalry heats up as Chinese models gain ground
title.zh: 中美人工智能竞争加剧，中国模型迎头赶上

summary.en: China's AI platforms are rapidly advancing, narrowing the gap with US technology. This progress has led to renewed threats from the Trump administration, alongside accusations of intellectual property theft, raising concerns about escalating tensions between the two nations.
summary.zh: 中国的人工智能平台正迅速缩小与美国同行的差距。这一进展引发了特朗普政府新的威胁，并伴随着知识产权盗窃的指控，令人担忧两国之间的紧张关系可能升级。

body.en:
China's AI platforms are rapidly closing the gap with their US counterparts, prompting fresh threats from the Trump administration. With accusations of intellectual property theft, could tensions boil over?

In what seems like the blink of an eye,  China has gone from being up to five years behind the United States in top-tier artificial intelligence (AI) to lagging by just a few months.

While US players, including Anthropic's Claude and OpenAI's ChatGPT , have spent hundreds of billions of dollars to push the frontier of AI, China has pursued a very different path .

Faced with US curbs on high-end chips that help AI to do its most advanced thinking, Chinese tech firms have prioritized dozens of open-source AI models built on "good enough"  technology .

These platforms, including DeepSeek, Alibaba's Qwen and Xiaomi's MiMo, are now widely deployed across Chinese businesses, government services and consumer devices.

In the latest sign of the gap closing, Chinese startup Moonshot AI last week unveiled Kimi K3, a model that rivals one of the most advanced AI models — Anthropic's Claude Fable 5 — on key benchmarks.

In some tests, Kimi K3 matches or even surpasses Claude with far less computing power and at a fraction of the cost. 

Global technology specialist Alvin W. Graylin thinks Kimi K3's arrival turns high-end AI from an expensive luxury into something practical and affordable.

"For 98% of customers, the 1 to 2% difference [in knowledge] isn't worth paying 10 to 20 times more."

China's latest advance has already drawn a strong reaction from Washington, with US President Donald Trump now threatening to block US access to Chinese AI models.

Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, meanwhile, warned earlier this week that the US could sanction Chinese models over alleged intellectual property (IP) theft.

Anthropic  and OpenAI have accused Chinese labs of using their models to train their own systems, a process known as distilling.

While distilling is a common practice by AI labs worldwide to a limited extent, the companies say their models have been bombarded with queries to harvest advanced reasoning. The White House warned in April that China was doing it on an "industrial scale."

Beijing has hit back, rejecting the accusations as baseless and calling US threats of sanctions and model bans "technological bullying" to contain China's rise.

Giulia Neaher, a research analyst at the Strategic Foresight Hub at the Washington-based Stimson Center think tank, downplayed the role of distilling in Kimi's progress.

body.zh: 中国的人工智能平台正在迅速缩小与美国同行的差距，引发了特朗普政府的新威胁。随着知识产权盗窃的指控，紧张局势会升级吗？ 似乎一眨眼的功夫，中国在顶级人工智能 (AI) 领域就从落后美国五年变为仅落后几个月。 尽管包括 Anthropic 的 Claude 和 OpenAI 的 ChatGPT 在内的美国企业已经花费了数千亿美元来推动人工智能的前沿发展，但中国却走了一条截然不同的道路。 面对美国对帮助人工智能实现最先进思维的高端芯片的限制，中国科技公司优先考虑了数十种基于“足够好”技术的开源人工智能模型。 这些平台，包括 DeepSeek、阿里巴巴的 Qwen 和小米的 MiMo，现已广泛部署在中国企业、政府服务和消费设备中。 作为缩小差距的最新迹象，中国初创公司 Moonshot AI 上周推出了 Kimi K3，该模型在关键基准测试上可与最先进的人工智能模型之一——Anthropic 的 Claude Fable 5 相媲美。 在某些测试中，Kimi K3 可以与 Claude 相媲美甚至超过 Claude，但其计算能力却要低得多，而成本却只是 Claude 的一小部分。 全球技术专家 Alvin W. Inflation has dropped to 3.8% in the year to June, from 4% in the previous month, with lower than anticipated underlying price pressures weighing against the chance of another Reserve Bank interest rate hike.

The unexpected drop in headline inflation by the monthly measure was married with a softer than expected 0.8% quarterly increase in the RBA’s preferred trimmed mean measure of price growth, the Australian Bureau of Statistics data showed.

body.en:
Victoria's new premier, Ben Carroll , has four months to claw back support for Labor ahead of the state election on 28 November.

"I will do things differently, because different times require a new approach," he told reporters on Tuesday.

He replaces former premier Jacinta Allan, once the youngest female parliamentarian when she was first elected at age 25, who took on the role of premier in 2023 following Daniel Andrews' resignation .

But Allan's reign as premier saw her net approval ratings plummet in recent months, as she faced mounting criticism over Labor's infrastructure spending and its response to alleged corruption in the construction industry.

An opinion poll conducted by Resolve indicated 43 per cent of Victorians prefer Liberal leader Jess Wilson for state premier, compared with 24 per cent who favour Allan.

Another poll, from RedBridge in July, put the once-popular Labor Party's primary vote at 26 per cent, behind One Nation's 27 per cent.

Ben Carroll's first act as premier was to announce a royal commission into the construction sector, which had been plagued by years of corruption scandals centred on the $109 billion 'Big Build' infrastructure program.

"In my government, integrity will not be optional," Carroll said in his first speech to the press on Tuesday afternoon.

The commission will focus on the Construction, Forestry and Maritime Employees Union (CFMEU), first alleged by the Nine Network in 2024 to have worked with crime organisations to profit from Big Build contracts.

According to the government's website, Big Build has delivered 130 infrastructure projects since 2015 at a cost of around $109 billion, including the controversial Suburban Rail Loop .

In February, an investigation commissioned by the CFMEU estimated Victorian taxpayers had lost $15 billion to organised crime, an untested figure which was disputed by Allan and the state's attorney-general at the time.

The same month, Victorian Liberals and Nationals pledged support for a royal commission.

Allan, who had referred Big Build to the state's anti-corruption watchdog in 2024, resisted calls for a royal commission despite her approval ratings plummeting amid perceived inaction over Big Build corruption.

One Resolve poll, published by Nine in July, had Allan's approval rating at -36 per cent.

As pressure mounted, Allan acknowledged and apologised for criminal conduct on Big Build in an op-ed in The Age in early July.

summary.en: Data centres would be forced to invest in additional renewable energy infrastructure in a bid to keep power prices down.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自澳洲栏目的新闻，重点涉及真理、分辨与诚实。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Large-scale data centres will be forced to invest in additional renewable energy to fuel their operations and avoid causing power price hikes in regulations agreed to by all but two states and territories.

The Energy and Climate Change Ministerial Council revealed its plans late on Tuesday after meeting to discuss advice on the issue from the Australian Energy Market Commission.

Climate groups welcomed the announcement and boost for renewable energy, but an organisation representing data centre operators warned the policy could be counterproductive if designed without their input.

The changes come weeks after Prime Minister Anthony Albanese announced plans to require data centres to be powered by clean energy projects under a shake-up of artificial intelligence rules , and after a NSW data centre inquiry heard similar calls for action.

The council, which includes energy ministers from the federal government and all state and territory governments, met virtually to discuss data centre energy proposals after flagging the issue in May.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

All ministers except those from Queensland and the Northern Territory agreed to pursue regulations that would "mandate that data centres offset their electricity demand by investing in additional renewable generation", the meeting communique said.

Renewable energy would need to be generated near the data centre unless local authorities opted out of the requirement, and the rules would be set at a national level, although states and territories could add additional requirements.

Changes to national rules would be considered in September, including reforms to the way data centres reported energy use.

The Climate Council called the proposed changes encouraging, although chief executive Amanda McKenzie said the rules should give data centre operators strict deadlines.

Governments from all Australian states and territories should also support the changes, she said, to avoid penalising some consumers with rising power bills.

"Unless these hold-out governments get on board, Queenslanders and Territorians will be left paying higher power bills, and we will all pay the price of higher climate pollution," she said.

But introducing a blanket rule for data centres' energy use could be ineffective if it was not designed with industry input, Data Centres Australia chief executive Belinda Dennett said.

body.en:
Offset accounts are often marketed as a simple way to reduce home loan interest, but a report by the Australian Securities and Investments Commission (ASIC) has found that some banks fail to deliver on that promise.

ASIC, Australia's financial services and consumer credit regulator, reviewed the offset practices of eight banks, which together represent more than 70 per cent of Australia's approximately $2.5 trillion home loan market .

It found that, while practices varied across these financial institutions — AMP, ANZ, CommBank, Great Southern Bank, HSBC Australia, ING, Macquarie Bank and Westpac — there were weaknesses in how they established, monitored and managed offset accounts.

It identified two cases where customers unknowingly paid more than $17,000 extra interest on their home loan because the bank did not make clear that offset accounts had to be re-linked after refinancing.

In another circumstance, a customer paid over $3,500 in additional interest over about a month after their account was incorrectly de-linked.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

Reports to ASIC between 1 September 2023 and 31 August 2025 showed banks paid more than $55 million in customer compensation for offset account failures.

It expects compensation to continue as banks further analyse offset account operations.

ASIC chair Sarah Court said that "when offset accounts don't operate correctly, the harm can be hidden".

"Loan repayments stay the same, while customers unknowingly pay more interest and take longer to repay their loan."

Hue Hwa Au Yong, a senior lecturer in banking and finance at Monash University, said offset accounts are "simple to understand but difficult for customers to verify".

Like an everyday transaction account, offset accounts can be used to deposit and withdraw money.

However, the amount of money in an offset account also reduces the outstanding amount owed on a home loan, which is used to calculate interest.

If a person has $50,000 in their offset account and a $750,000 loan, they will only be charged interest on $700,000.

"So, the issue really is not the product itself, but the system behind it," Yong told SBS News.

"As a bank customer, we can see how much money is in our offset account. But as a borrower, we can't easily verify whether the banking systems are correctly applying it when calculating interest, [which] ... is calculated daily using a quite complex formula and system. "

Australian Banking Association CEO Simon Birmingham told SBS News that offset accounts "can be an effective way for mortgage holders to save on interest and in more than 99 per cent of cases banks were found to manage them correctly".

Watch Insight episode Housemates on SBS On Demand.

When Charlotte, 26, was a university student, she moved in with a man who was also her landlord .

Her first impression of him was positive, but she says she moved in "without being fully aware of what that individual was like".

"He came across as very easy to get on with … relatively nonchalant, had a good job, communicated well," she told Insight.

"I noticed that there were belongings that weren't present when I had viewed the property, such as Bibles, that were being left around the apartment.

She explained that, although she likes to think he was motivated by "good intentions", his placement of the cross made her uncomfortable; it felt like an invasion of her privacy and imposition of his beliefs onto her.

Charlotte says the final straw came when the landlord's family visited the apartment.

"They said: 'We've heard so much about you. We can't believe that he's found someone.'"

At first, she thought they were pleased he'd filled his vacant room — but that wasn't the case.

Charlotte says that later, when she raised this issue with the landlord, he shut down and stopped communicating entirely.

Shortly after, she returned to the apartment to find the locks had been changed.

Luckily, Charlotte was able to call a friend who put her up until she found a new place.

When one of Holly's housemates moved out of their four-person share house, a friend-of-a-friend replaced them as a subtenant.

While Holly admits she wasn't always the perfect housemate and was probably "very naggy", she says they "should have vetted [the new subtenant] a little bit harder".

"He would leave pee all over the toilet seat consistently," the 25-year-old says.

"He let his ceiling get, like, 70 per cent black mould coverage, going, 'Oh, sorry, I thought it was a shadow.'"

Holly says the subtenant was unresponsive when she raised concerns about pulling his weight in the house.

"If someone says, 'Oh, yeah, no worries, I'll do it' and then they don't do it, there's only so many times you can kind of ask them before you just start to feel crazy."

title.en: Gina Rinehart funded flights and fashion show for Pauline Hanson
title.zh: 吉娜·莱因哈特 (Gina Rinehart) 资助宝琳·汉森 (Pauline Hanson) 的航班和时装秀

summary.en: While Gina Rinehart supported her trip, the One Nation leader said she paid for accommodation, meals and daily expenses.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自澳洲栏目的新闻，重点涉及对脆弱群体的怜悯。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Mining magnate Gina Rinehart flew One Nation leader Pauline Hanson around Europe and paid for her tickets to a luxury fashion show while she was there.

Hanson's flights from London to Sicily via Rome, and back again, were all funded by Rinehart, the senator's parliamentary register of interests revealed after being updated on Tuesday.

However, Hanson reported paying for accommodation, meals and daily expenses herself during the trip, which took place between 11 and 16 July, as first reported by Fairfax outlets.

Hanson drew criticism after she and Rinehart were sighted at a luxury Italian resort and attending a Dolce and Gabbana fashion event in Sicily.

Questioned when she returned to Australia, Hanson did not go into detail on how the bill was split, but insisted taxpayers had not paid for the luxury weekend.

"It didn't cost the taxpayer one cent for my trip overseas. Not one cent," she told a Seven West Media event last week.

Hanson, who was also gifted a private plane by Rinehart in April, defended her billionaire friend , who inherited Hancock Prospecting from her late father, saying she had "done it tough".

"She had to borrow everything and was flat out in the very start to pay the bills. She's built up that company," she said.

On Monday, Hanson lost an appeal over a Federal Court finding she had made a racist remark towards deputy Greens leader Mehreen Faruqi.

In response to a post on social media soon after the death of Queen Elizabeth II in 2022, Hanson told Faruqi to "piss off back to Pakistan".

In his initial decision handed down in 2024, justice Angus Stewart ruled the post was "seriously offensive" and a "strong form of racism".

Hanson said she was disappointed by Monday's outcome and was considering lodging a final appeal in the High Court.

"Public discussion in Australia has become almost totally silenced by laws and rules which prevent ordinary people expressing their personal views in case some small part of our society takes some sort of offence or feels hurt or 'distressed'," she said in a statement.

title.en: Australia has a favourite day to say 'I do' — but fewer couples are saying it
title.zh: 澳大利亚人最喜欢的结婚日期——以及新的婚姻数据揭示了什么

summary.en: New data indicates a decline in marriage rates across Australia, accompanied by a slight increase in the divorce rate.
summary.zh: 新数据显示，澳大利亚的结婚率有所下降，而离婚率则略有上升。

body.en:
Saturday 25 October was Australia's favourite day to say "I do" in 2025 — but new data suggests fewer couples are saying it.

Fewer Australians tied the knot last year than the year before, according to new figures from the Australian Bureau of Statistics.

At the same time, more marriages are coming to an end, with the divorce rate ticking upward for the first time in several years, though ultimately remaining lower than it was 20 years ago.

The most popular wedding date in 2025 was Saturday 25 October — i.e. the symmetrical 25/10/25 — with 2,035 marriages.

That's about 500 more than the runner-up, Saturday 22 November (22/11/25) — which had 1,527.

ABS data show there's somewhat of a trend towards more marriages on dates with numerical significance, though for some it could also be coincidence.

The least popular days were Christmas Day, with 51 weddings, Boxing Day with 54, New Year's Day with 57, and Tuesday 29 July with 61.

Spring dominated the wedding calendar, with most of the top ten dates falling in September, October and November. The rest were scattered across autumn.

Saturday remains, unsurprisingly, the nation's preferred wedding day — more than 52,000 marriages took place on a Saturday in 2025, and 45 of the year's most popular dates fell on one.

Friday came in second, with just over 21,000 marriages, led by Friday 10 October (10/10/25).

Zoom out further, and one day still reigns supreme: 10 November 2012 — the sequential 10/11/12.

That remains the most popular wedding date of the past 20 years, with 3,081 marriages recorded on that day — still comfortably ahead of the runner-up, 11 November 2011 (11/11/11), which had 2,614.

Beyond the calendar quirks, the broader numbers tell a clearer story: marriage is becoming less common in Australia.

There were 118,804 marriages registered in 2025 — 2,040 fewer than in 2024, a drop of 1.7 per cent.

That's in line with 2023's total (118,439), but still well above the pandemic-era lows of 2020 and 2021.

Adjusted for population, the marriage rate — the number of marriages per 1,000 people aged 16 and over — fell slightly to 5.3 in 2025, down from 5.5 in both 2023 and 2024.

Zoom out to 2005, where the marriage rate was 6.9, and the decline is even more stark.

The biggest drops came among 25-29 and 30-34 year-olds. No age group recorded an increase.

Despite the falling numbers, the age at which Australians marry has barely moved: 32.7 years for men (down marginally from 32.8 in 2024) and 31.2 years for women, unchanged for the third year running.
